title: Upgrade clears derived caches and preserves user data
question_or_target: Does `update` / `install --repair` invalidate exactly the caches it owns while leaving user data untouched? PASS requires an explicit ownership manifest for cache paths; anything not on it must survive the upgrade byte-identical.

evidence.claim: Independent reviewer verified the artifact at command-center/receipts/TST-0175.json exists on disk (26049 LF-normalized bytes), parses as JSON, carried the builder terminal state=BLOCKED with failure.classification=[reviewer-absent] and reviewer=null (no self-certification) at review time, and its report.kind=cache_report matches the catalog output_schema pin.

Receipt rewritten from the builder BLOCKED pointer into receipt-core shape; the original builder document is preserved verbatim under extensions.builder_receipt_original. The receipt self-row is role=supporting and carries the PRE-closure builder bytes sha256; the authoritative post-closure registration is the UNIT-ARTIFACT-MANIFEST row, refreshed by the reviewer to the final closure bytes (see extensions.reviewer_manifest_refresh).
